title: TTS voice id "af" does not exist in Xybrid's kokoro-82m (Kokoro v1.0), so every read-aloud attempt fails
scenario: Turn on 'Read replies aloud' and send any message. After the agent finishes, speak() downloads and loads kokoro-82m, then runs model.runAsync(envelope: .text(text: chunk, voiceId: "af", speed: 1.0)). The Kokoro v1.0 bundle has no voice called "af", so the run throws and the status bar shows 'Speech failed: Voice 'af' not found. Available voices: [...]'. This happens on every reply, so read-aloud never works, and the 183 MB model download on first use is wasted.
evidence: App: `static let ttsVoice = "af"` (line 18), passed at line 160 as `XybridEnvelope.text(text: chunk, voiceId: Self.ttsVoice, speed: 1.0)`. The registry entry (GET https://registry.xybrid.dev/v1/models/kokoro-82m) has hf_repo xybrid-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX and `"voices":{"default":"af_heart","catalog":[af_heart, af_alloy, af_aoede, af_bella, ... bm_daniel]}`, with no "af". The pinned voices.bin (revision 018ebc3b...) is an NPZ (it starts with PK and an af_alloy.npy entry). Its central directory lists 54 *.npy names and none is af.npy. In Xybrid v0.21.0 crates/xybrid-core/src/execution/voice_loader.rs, resolve_voice_info does `metadata.get_voice(vid).ok_or_else(|| AdapterError::InvalidInput(format!("Voice '{}' not found. Available voices: {:?}", ...)))`. get_voice is an exact match (`.find(|v| v.id == voice_id)`). The legacy path `load_by_name` returns `VoiceError::VoiceNotFound`. The Xybrid iOS example only uses "af" as a placeholder: after load it sets `self.voiceId = loadedModel.defaultVoice()?.id`.
fix: Use `"af_heart"` (the catalog default). Better: pass `voiceId: nil` so the model default is used, or resolve it once with `model.defaultVoice()?.id` after load.

The zero-embedding fallback only applies when the voice file is missing, which is not the case here.

4. **"af" matches nothing in either lookup path in voice_loader.rs.**
   - Config path: resolve_voice_info calls `metadata.get_voice(vid)`. In metadata.rs:641 that is an exact match (`.find(|v| v.id == voice_id)`), and the error is "Voice '{}' not found. Available voices: ...".

**Result:** with read-aloud on, every speak() call downloads and loads the model, then the first runAsync throws. The error is caught and lastError is set to "Speech failed: ...", so read-aloud never produces audio. Severity high is fair: the feature is completely broken, though no data is lost. | fix: Change ios/AgentConsole/Speech/SpeechService.swift:18 to `static let ttsVoice: String? = nil` and pass it as voiceId, so the model's catalog default (af_heart) is used. title: Pressing Stop mid-answer makes the app read the truncated reply aloud
scenario: Read-aloud is on and the agent is streaming a long answer. The user taps Stop. LocalAgent.stop() cancels the task. The consumer is suspended in `for try await chunk in conversation.send(message)`, and an AsyncThrowingStream returns nil when its consuming task is cancelled (stdlib _Storage.next uses onCancel: cancel(), which finishes the stream). The loop therefore exits normally, so neither `try Task.checkCancellation()` in the body nor the `catch is CancellationError` that appends the 'Stopped.' error turn runs. `guard let call = ToolCallParser.firstCall(in: reply) else { return }` returns normally and the partial assistant turn stays last. isRunning goes false, and the hook speaks the half-finished answer the user just stopped.
evidence: SpeechControls.swift:69-73 `onChange(of: agent.isRunning) { _, running in if running { ... stopSpeaking() } else if let last = agent.turns.last, last.role == .assistant { SpeechService.shared.speakIfEnabled(last.text) } }`. LocalAgent.swift:86-91 `for try await chunk in conversation.send(message) { try Task.checkCancellation() ... } guard let call = ToolCallParser.firstCall(in: reply) else { return }`. mlx-swift-lm 3.33 ChatSession.streamMap builds the stream with `AsyncThrowingStream<R, Error>.makeStream()` (continuation-based), so consumer cancellation returns nil instead of throwing.
fix: In the hook, skip speaking when the run was cancelled. For example, have LocalAgent record a `lastRunCancelled` flag, or call `try Task.checkCancellation()` right after the stream loop so a cancelled run always ends with the 'Stopped.' error turn.
verifier_notes:
UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. I re-read the code at origin/xybrid-speech and the described path runs as claimed in the common case.

1. LocalAgent.stop() (Inference/LocalAgent.swift:38) only calls task?.cancel(). The send() task always reaches `self?.isRunning = false` after run() returns (lines 44-47), however run() exits.
2. MLXConversation.send (Inference/MLXBackend.swift:56-57) returns ChatSession.streamResponse directly. In mlx-swift-lm 3.33.0, streamResponse goes through streamMap, which builds the stream with `AsyncThrowingStream<R, Error>.makeStream()` (ChatSession.swift:1164). Its onTermination only cancels the producer task on `.cancelled` (ChatSession.swift:2074-2079). The stream is continuation-based.
3. The stdlib's AsyncThrowingStream.next() wraps the wait in withTaskCancellationHandler with onCancel calling cancel(). cancel() runs onTermination(.cancelled) and then finish(). With nothing buffered, the waiting continuation resumes with nil and no error. Token generation is much slower than the main-actor loop body (append plus a turns update, with no suspension point), so the consumer is almost always parked in next() with an empty buffer when Stop is tapped. The `for try await` loop at LocalAgent.swift:86-90 then ends normally. The checkCancellation inside the loop (line 87) never runs, and the `catch is CancellationError` that appends "Stopped." (lines 107-108) is never reached.
4. `guard let call = ToolCallParser.firstCall(in: reply) else { return }` (line 91) returns normally for a partial prose reply. The last turn is still the partial `.assistant` turn.
5. ChatView.swift:45 applies `.speechReadsReplies(agent)`. On isRunning going false, SpeechControls.swift:69-73 finds `turns.last` with role .assistant and calls speakIfEnabled(last.text). When read-aloud is on, speakIfEnabled (SpeechService.swift:142-145) only checks speakReplies and then speaks the truncated text.

There are only narrow exceptions where "Stopped." does get appended:
- A chunk was already buffered: next() returns it, and the body's checkCancellation throws.
- The producer task's finish(throwing:) sets the terminal state before cancel()'s own finish() does, which is an unlikely cross-thread race.

Neither happens in the typical streaming case. The defect is real: tapping Stop mid-answer reads the half-finished reply aloud, which works against the user's intent. Medium or low severity is fair, since nothing is lost or exposed. | fix: In LocalAgent.run, call `try Task.checkCancellation()` right after the `for try await chunk in conversation.send(message)` loop, before `ToolCallParser.firstCall`. A cancelled run then always ends in the `catch is CancellationError` branch, which appends the `.error` "Stopped." turn. Because the last turn is no longer `.assistant`, the speechReadsReplies hook stays silent. This also stops a cancelled run from treating a partial reply as complete, for example by parsing and running a tool call from it.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this. Every piece of the claim checks out against the origin/xybrid-speech code.

1. **The Stop path.** ChatView.swift:32 Stop only calls `agent.stop()`, which is `task?.cancel()` (LocalAgent.swift:38). Nothing else stops speech.

2. **Where the stream comes from.** MLXBackend.swift:56-57 returns `session.streamResponse(to:)`. In mlx-swift-lm 3.33.0, ChatSession.swift:1164 builds that stream with `AsyncThrowingStream<R, Error>.makeStream()`, and `continuation.onTermination` (line 2074) cancels the generator.

3. **What the stdlib does on cancel.** AsyncThrowingStream's `next()` wraps its wait in `withTaskCancellationHandler { ... } onCancel: { cancel() }`. `cancel()` fires onTermination(.cancelled) and then `finish()`, which resumes the pending continuation with nil. So a consumer cancelled while waiting in `next()` sees the stream end normally, with no error.

4. **The agent loop exits as a success.** In LocalAgent.run (lines ~86-91), the `for try await` loop ends. The `try Task.checkCancellation()` inside the loop body never runs, because no further chunk arrives. Next, `guard let call = ToolCallParser.firstCall(in: reply) else { return }` returns normally, since a truncated prose reply has no tool call. The `catch is CancellationError` that would append the "Stopped." error turn is skipped. The partial assistant turn stays as `turns.last`.

5. **The hook speaks it.** The Task in `send()` sets `isRunning = false`. The hook at SpeechControls.swift:69-73 sees running == false and a last turn with role == .assistant, and calls `speakIfEnabled(last.text)`. That function only checks `speakReplies` (SpeechService.swift:142-145) and then calls `speak()`, which synthesizes the text. There is no "was cancelled" guard anywhere.

**One nuance: it is timing-dependent.** It does not happen on every Stop. `stop()` runs on the main actor, so the run task is never mid-body at that moment. It is either suspended inside `next()` or queued to resume with a chunk it already received.
- In the queued case, the loop-body `checkCancellation()` throws and the user correctly gets "Stopped.".
- In the suspended case, which is common because each token takes tens of milliseconds to generate while the main-actor hop is brief, the partial reply is read aloud.

So the defect is real and intermittent. It also undermines Stop: the user taps it to silence a long answer, and the half answer is spoken anyway. Medium severity is reasonable. | fix: In LocalAgent.run, call `try Task.checkCancellation()` right after the `for try await chunk in conversation.send(message)` loop and before `ToolCallParser.firstCall`. A cancelled run then always lands in `catch is CancellationError`, which appends the "Stopped." error turn, and the speech hook skips it because the last turn is no longer .assistant. Optionally, also have the hook (or `stop()`) call `SpeechService.shared.stopSpeaking()`, and skip speaking when the agent records a `lastRunCancelled` flag.

1. In ChatView.swift:32 on origin/xybrid-speech, the Stop button calls agent.stop(). LocalAgent.swift:38 implements that as `task?.cancel()`. The cancelled task is the MainActor Task created in send() at lines 44-47.

Medium severity fits: it is a user-visible wrong action with no data loss. | fix: In LocalAgent.run, add `try Task.checkCancellation()` right after the `for try await chunk in conversation.send(message) { ... }` loop, before `guard let call = ToolCallParser.firstCall(in: reply)`. A cancelled run then always throws CancellationError and appends the `.error` 'Stopped.' turn, so `turns.last.role != .assistant` and the speech hook skips it. This also fixes the pre-existing missing 'Stopped.' message. For defense in depth, you can also expose a `private(set) var lastRunCancelled` flag set in the CancellationError catch, and have speechReadsReplies check it before calling speakIfEnabled.

title: Cancelling read-aloud during the first-use model download or load leaves phase stuck at .loading, which disables the mic; the download keeps running
scenario: First reply with read-aloud on: phase becomes .downloading(kokoro-82m). The user turns the speaker toggle off (didSet calls stopSpeaking) or sends another message (the hook calls stopSpeaking). stopSpeaking cancels speakTask but only resets phase when it is .speaking or .synthesizing. In the cancelled task, the `for await status in download.progress()` loop ends (AsyncStream returns nil on cancellation), and then `phase = .loading(model:)` and `try await loader.load()` run. Xybrid's load() is `Task.detached { try loadSync() }`, which ignores cancellation, so it keeps downloading 183 MB and loads the model. The task then throws CancellationError at checkCancellation, and `if !Task.isCancelled { self.phase = .idle }` is skipped. phase stays .loading, so isBusy is true and SpeechMicButton stays disabled (`speech.isBusy && !speech.isRecording`) with a permanent 'Loading kokoro-82m...' spinner. With the toggle off, nothing ever resets it until relaunch. If speak() is called again before the first load finishes, `tts` is still nil, so a second concurrent loadModel/load of the same model starts (double download, double memory).
evidence: Line 36 `if !speakReplies { stopSpeaking() }`. Line 180 `if phase == .speaking || phase == .synthesizing { phase = .idle }`. Lines 67-78 `if needsDownload(id), let download = loader.download() { phase = .downloading(...); for await status in download.progress() {...} } phase = .loading(model: id); return try await loader.load()`. Line 170 `if !Task.isCancelled { self.phase = .idle }`. Xybrid.swift:426-428 `public func load() async throws -> XybridModel { try await Task.detached { try loadSync() }.value }`. ttsModel() (lines 87-92) has no in-flight de-duplication.
fix: Reset phase in stopSpeaking for .downloading and .loading too (or always set `phase = .idle` in the task's cancellation path). Keep the XybridDownload and call `download.cancel()` on cancellation. Memoize the in-flight load as a `Task<XybridModel, Error>` so concurrent callers share one load.
verifier_notes:
UPHELD(high): I couldn't refute this. I checked it against origin/xybrid-speech ios/AgentConsole/Speech/SpeechService.swift and the local copy of Xybrid.swift.

1. **What resets phase.** stopSpeaking() (line 174-181) cancels speakTask and sets it to nil. It only moves phase back to .idle when phase is .speaking or .synthesizing (line 180). In this scenario phase is .downloading or .loading, so stopSpeaking leaves it alone.

2. **How the task ends.** Inside the cancelled task, loadModel (lines 64-79) leaves the download.progress() loop. The Xybrid docs at Xybrid.swift:472-473 say "Cancelling the task consuming `progress()` unsubscribes from updates; call XybridDownload/cancel() to stop the transfer itself". So the loop ends, but the transfer keeps going, because the app never calls download.cancel(). The code then sets `phase = .loading(model: id)` (line 77) and awaits loader.load(). That call is `Task.detached { try loadSync() }` (Xybrid.swift:426-428), which does not respond to cancellation. It finishes, and tts is assigned. The first `try Task.checkCancellation()` (line 157) then throws CancellationError, which is caught at line 166. Line 170, `if !Task.isCancelled { self.phase = .idle }`, is skipped. If load throws something else instead, the generic catch also skips both lastError and the reset. Either way, phase stays .loading or .downloading.

3. **Effect on the UI.** isBusy (lines 41-46) is true for those phases. SpeechMicButton is `.disabled(speech.isBusy && !speech.isRecording)` (SpeechControls.swift), and SpeechStatusBar keeps showing the "Loading kokoro-82m…" or "Downloading…" spinner.

4. **Nothing else clears it.** The only other places that write phase are startRecording (unreachable, because the button is disabled), stopRecordingAndTranscribe, cancelRecording (only from .recording), and a new speak() task. speak() is reached only through speakIfEnabled, from the speechReadsReplies onChange hook. With the toggle off it never runs, and turning the toggle back on does not call speak. So the stuck state lasts until relaunch, or until a later reply arrives with the toggle on.

5. **Both triggers are real.** The toggle's didSet calls stopSpeaking (line 36), and the onChange hook calls stopSpeaking whenever agent.isRunning becomes true.

6. **Double load.** ttsModel() (lines 88-93) only checks `tts`, and that is assigned after the load finishes. A second speak() before the first load completes therefore starts a second loadModel/load of the same model.

Severity medium is reasonable: there is no data loss, but speech input is disabled with a permanent spinner, and a 183 MB download plus model memory are spent without anything using them. | fix: Make cancellation always restore the phase. In speak()'s task, replace line 170 with an unconditional reset that only applies while this task is still the current speakTask. For example, capture a token or compare task identity, then `self.phase = .idle` on every exit path, or use a defer. Separately, in stopSpeaking(), also reset .downloading and .loading to .idle. Keep the XybridDownload in loadModel and call download.cancel() from a withTaskCancellationHandler. Memoize the in-flight TTS and ASR loads as a stored `Task<XybridModel, Error>` so concurrent callers await one shared load instead of starting a second one.

UPHELD(high): The defect is real; I could not refute it. On origin/xybrid-speech, SpeechService.swift:174-181 `stopSpeaking()` cancels speakTask and sets phase back to .idle only when it is .speaking or .synthesizing. The cancelled task's only reset is line 170, `if !Task.isCancelled { self.phase = .idle }`. That line is skipped for a cancelled task on every path: the CancellationError catch, the generic catch (also guarded), and normal exit. So if the task is cancelled while phase is .downloading (line 68/70) or .loading (line 77), phase stays there.

The Xybrid source I checked locally (scratchpad/xybrid/Xybrid.swift:426-428 and 451-473) confirms the rest:
- `load()` is `try await Task.detached { try loadSync() }.value`. A detached task does not inherit cancellation, so the load and any download inside it run to completion.
- The doc comment on `download()` says that cancelling the task that consumes `progress()` (an AsyncStream, xybrid_bolt.swift:4136) only unsubscribes, and you must call `XybridDownload.cancel()` to stop the transfer. SpeechService never calls it. So the cancelled task drops out of the for-await loop, sets phase = .loading, and runs the full load. ttsModel then stores `tts`. The task then throws at `checkCancellation` (line 157), and line 170 is skipped.

Both triggers are real:
- The SpeakerToggle `didSet` calls `stopSpeaking()` (line 36).
- `speechReadsReplies` calls `stopSpeaking()` when `agent.isRunning` turns true (SpeechControls.swift:71). The text-field send works while TTS is downloading.

Effect: `isBusy` is true for .downloading/.loading, so SpeechMicButton stays disabled (`.disabled(speech.isBusy && !speech.isRecording)`) and SpeechStatusBar keeps showing the 'Loading kokoro-82m…' spinner. Nothing else resets phase:
- `startRecording` can't run because the button is disabled.
- `cancelRecording` only resets .recording.

With the toggle off, this lasts until relaunch. With the toggle on, a later `speak()` recovers it, because that task eventually reaches line 170 uncancelled. title: No interruption, route-change or engine-configuration handling: interrupted playback hangs the speak task and capture stops silently

(b) During recording, plugging in or unplugging a headset or USB mic posts AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange and the engine stops itself. - The catch at lines 127-131 sets lastError, sets phase to `.idle` and returns "". `pcm` is a local variable, so the audio is gone once the function returns.

Nothing loads the model ahead of time. A `git grep` across ios/ on the branch shows startRecording() (lines 98-113) never calls asrModel() or loadModel(). The only callers are SpeechControls.swift lines 12 and 15, which call startRecording and stopRecordingAndTranscribe. There is no warm-up or prefetch anywhere else.

So on first use, while offline, recording up to 2 minutes and tapping stop loses the whole recording. The same loss happens on any transcription failure, including a failed load or a failed runAsync. Low severity is right: it is a usability and data-loss problem, but the data is a re-recordable voice clip. | fix: Load the model before capture, keep the audio after a failure, or do both:
1. In startRecording(), when `asr == nil`, start loading the model in the background (or wait for it first if needsDownload(asrModelId)), so a failed download shows up before the user speaks.
2. In stopRecordingAndTranscribe(), store the audio in a property such as `private var pendingPCM: [Int16]?` before transcribing. Clear it only after a successful transcript, and add a retryTranscription() that reuses it.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim; it holds. I checked origin/xybrid-speech.

- In ios/AgentConsole/Speech/SpeechService.swift, `stopRecordingAndTranscribe` (line 116) calls `recorder.stop()` at line 117 and keeps the PCM only in the local `pcm`.
- It then awaits `asrModel()` at line 120, which calls `loadModel(whisper-tiny-ggml)`. If the model is not cached (`needsDownload` is true), the download starts at that point, after the recording has ended.
- A failed download (`status.state == .failed` throws `SpeechError.downloadFailed` at line 72) or a failing `loader.load()` (line 78) lands in the catch at lines 127-131. That sets `lastError`, sets `phase = .idle` and returns "". Nothing keeps `pcm` for a retry.
- `startRecording()` (lines 98-113) only asks for mic permission, sets up the audio session and starts the recorder. It never prefetches or loads the ASR model.
- `git grep` found only one caller, SpeechMicButton in SpeechControls.swift:12. On an empty transcript it does nothing, so the user has to record again.
- Nothing else in the branch warms the model up at launch or when the view appears. The only references to `asrModel` or `needsDownload` are inside SpeechService itself.

So on first use, recording while offline or on a flaky connection loses the whole recording when the download fails. Severity is low: it is a usability and data-loss problem that only happens on first use, and the user can record again once the model is cached. | fix: Pick one of these:
1. In `startRecording()`, when `needsDownload(Self.asrModelId)` is true, kick off `Task { _ = try? await asrModel() }` before capture starts, or await the download first. Note that `loadModel` overwrites `phase` while it runs, so the `.downloading`/`.loading` phases must not override `.recording`. Order the phase updates accordingly, or block recording until the model is ready.
2. Keep the PCM in a `private var pendingPCM: [Int16]?` that is set before `asrModel()` and cleared only on success. Then add a `retryTranscription()` that runs the stored buffer again after a failure.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute the claim. On origin/xybrid-speech, line 117 of SpeechService.swift (`let pcm = recorder.stop()`) drains the buffer. MicRecorder.stop() copies `samples` into a local and then sets `samples = []`. The ASR model is loaded only after that, in asrModel() at line 120, through loadModel(), which downloads it when needsDownload is true. If the download fails (SpeechError.downloadFailed, or any error from download or load), the catch at lines 127-131 sets lastError, sets phase to .idle and returns "". `pcm` is a local variable and is never stored anywhere, so the recording is lost. Nothing in the branch loads the model early. A git grep shows asrModel is called only from stopRecordingAndTranscribe, startRecording does not touch the model, and nothing warms it at launch. SpeechControls only calls startRecording and stopRecordingAndTranscribe. Failing case: whisper-tiny-ggml is not cached, the user records a long message, taps stop while offline, the download fails, the recording is gone and the user has to say it again. This is low severity and the claim was filed as low: it only happens on first use, the user gets an error message, and nothing that was saved is lost. | fix: Load the model before recording starts. Begin loading asrModel() in startRecording() (or in the background when the app launches), or keep the last PCM buffer in a property (for example `private var pendingPCM: [Int16]?`) when transcription fails, so the user can retry without recording again.

title: Speech models stay resident next to the LLM for the app's lifetime and are never released under memory pressure
scenario: After one dictation and one read-aloud, `asr` and `tts` hold whisper-tiny and Kokoro (registry: fp16 ONNX, weights_mb 170, plus the ORT arena). They are never unloaded, and Xybrid.releaseMemory() and setAutoRelease(true) are never wired. On a memory warning while Qwen3-1.7B is generating or a document batch is running, only MLX holds reclaimable cache, so the process is more likely to hit jetsam. Both the cancel/re-speak race and concurrent speak calls can transiently load a second Kokoro instance.
evidence: Lines 48-49 `private var asr: XybridModel?` and `private var tts: XybridModel?`, which are set once and never cleared. `git grep releaseMemory|didReceiveMemoryWarning origin/xybrid-speech -- ios` finds nothing. Xybrid.swift:122-139 documents `releaseMemory()` as the hook to wire to the platform low-memory signal (released models reload automatically on next use).
fix: Observe UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification and call `Xybrid.releaseMemory()` (or set `asr`/`tts` to nil). Consider `Xybrid.setAutoRelease(true)` after initialize().
verifier_notes:
UPHELD(medium): I checked the code at origin/xybrid-speech and the facts in the claim hold. In ios/AgentConsole/Speech/SpeechService.swift, `asr` and `tts` (lines 48-49) are set only inside asrModel() and ttsModel(). Nothing ever sets them back to nil, and SpeechService is a process-lifetime singleton (`static let shared`). `git grep` over origin/xybrid-speech -- ios for releaseMemory, didReceiveMemoryWarning, memoryWarning, setAutoRelease, `asr = nil` and `tts = nil` returns nothing. The only memory handling in the app is `MLX.Memory.cacheLimit` in MLXBackend.swift:27.

The local copy of the Xybrid SDK confirms the missing hook. Xybrid.swift:122-139 documents releaseMemory() as the call to wire to the platform low-memory signal; released models reload on their next use. Xybrid.swift:141-147 says setAutoRelease is "Off by default". So once the user has dictated once and had one reply read aloud, both models stay loaded alongside the MLX LLM, and on memory pressure the SDK will not free them by itself.

The double-load path is also real. speak() calls stopSpeaking(), which cancels the earlier speakTask. If that task is still waiting in `loader.load()`, it is not marked as loaded until it returns (`tts` is assigned only after the await). The new task then finds `tts == nil` and starts a second load of Kokoro, so two copies can exist for a short time. Whichever load finishes last overwrites `tts`, and the other copy is dropped.

Why this stays low severity: I could not show that the extra resident memory (about 75 MB for whisper-tiny plus about 170 MB for Kokoro fp16 and its ORT arena) actually triggers jetsam. The app also has the increased-memory-limit entitlement. That part of the impact is a plausible risk, not something I demonstrated. Still, the missing release path is concrete and the claim does not overstate it. | fix: In SpeechService.init, observe UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification. In the handler, when phase is .idle, call `_ = Xybrid.releaseMemory()` (it skips models with a run in flight, and released models reload on their next use), or set `asr` and `tts` to nil. Optionally call `Xybrid.setAutoRelease(true)` after Xybrid.initialize(). To stop the duplicate Kokoro load, store the in-flight load in a `Task<XybridModel, Error>?` (for example `ttsLoad`), and have ttsModel() await that existing task instead of starting a new loader.load().

UPHELD(medium): I could not refute the claim. On origin/xybrid-speech, ios/AgentConsole/Speech/SpeechService.swift:48-49 declares `private var asr: XybridModel?` and `private var tts: XybridModel?`. They are assigned once, in asrModel() and ttsModel(), and nothing in the file ever sets them back to nil or calls unload()/unloadAsync(). SpeechService is a process-lifetime singleton (`static let shared`), so whatever it loads stays resident until the app exits.

A case-insensitive `git grep` over ios on that branch for releaseMemory, memoryWarning and autoRelease finds nothing. No memory-warning observer exists anywhere in the app that could free the speech models indirectly.

The local Xybrid.swift source (scratchpad/xybrid/Xybrid.swift:122-153) confirms the claim's API reading. `releaseMemory()` is documented as the hook to wire to the platform low-memory signal. `setAutoRelease` is documented as "Off by default", so the SDK does not release idle models on its own under memory pressure.

The transient double-load also holds. speak() calls stopSpeaking() and then starts a new Task. If the cancelled task is still suspended inside `loadModel` (`await loader.load()`), `tts` is still nil, so the new task begins a second Kokoro load. Nothing checks for cancellation between load() returning and `tts = m`. I did not verify whether Xybrid deduplicates loads internally. Even if it does not, the extra instance is short-lived.

The impact is genuinely low. whisper-tiny plus Kokoro is a few hundred MB next to the MLX LLM, so this only raises jetsam risk under memory pressure; it is not deterministic data loss or a crash. The defect itself is real and backed by evidence. | fix: In SpeechService.init (or on first loadModel), add an observer for UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification. When it fires and phase is .idle, set `asr = nil` and `tts = nil`, then call `_ = Xybrid.releaseMemory()`. Releasing only when idle avoids pulling a model out from under an in-flight runAsync. Optionally call `Xybrid.setAutoRelease(true)` right after `Xybrid.initialize()`. To prevent the double load, keep a single in-flight `Task<XybridModel, Error>` per model id and await it, rather than starting a new load whenever `tts == nil`.

REFUTED(medium): The facts in the claim are accurate, but there is no concrete failure behind them. On origin/xybrid-speech, SpeechService.swift:48-49 does keep `asr` and `tts` cached once they load, and nothing in ios/ calls releaseMemory, setAutoRelease or didReceiveMemoryWarning. That is a deliberate lazy-load-and-keep cache, not a logic error. Nothing in the app handles memory warnings at all, MLX included. The only memory policy is `MLX.Memory.cacheLimit = 32 MB` in MLXBackend.swift:27, so the claim's line that "only MLX holds reclaimable cache" adds nothing. project.yml also sets `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit: true`. The extra resident memory (about 75 MB for whisper-tiny plus about 170 MB for Kokoro and the ORT arena) is small next to a Qwen3-1.7B footprint on an iPadOS 26 device with that entitlement. The claim gives no inputs or device state that lead to a jetsam kill or any wrong output. It only says such a kill becomes "more likely", which is a tuning suggestion, not a defect.

The side point about a second Kokoro load during a cancel or a concurrent speak() is possible. If a new speak() call starts while an earlier task is still awaiting loadModel, `tts` is still nil, so the model loads twice. That cost is brief and bounded. Whichever load finishes last overwrites `tts`, and ARC frees the other copy, so there is no lasting leak or wrong behavior. I could not build a scenario that ends in a crash, lost data or wrong output. Following the default-to-refute rule, this is refuted: at most it is an optional hardening idea of wiring a memory-warning observer.
